citation.authors: Reed KS, Crew MR, Frescoln AM, Romanowski SM, Valentine RJ, Lefferts WK
citation.title: Effects of a high-sugar mixed meal on cerebrovascular haemodynamics in young, healthy versus middle-aged adults with cardiometabolic risk factors

reported.what: plasma glucose at baseline, 30 and 60 min after the 930 kcal high-sugar mixed meal (129 g carbohydrate, 35.5 g fat, 14 g protein), young healthy group (n = 21) and middle-aged group, as mean ± an unlabelled spread (Table 2; its footnote gives only abbreviations and time-effect symbols)

location.where: Table 2, row 'Glucose, mg/dL', YA, columns BL, 30 min, 60 min

reported.what: plasma insulin at the same times and groups, printed in pg/mL (a unit the loader does not accept; the paper gives no conversion), same unlabelled ± (Table 2)

location.where: Table 2, row 'Insulin, pg/mL', YA, columns BL, 30 min, 60 min

reported.what: heart rate at baseline, 30 and 60 min, both groups, same unlabelled ± (Table 3; footnote gives only abbreviations and significance symbols)

location.where: Table 3, row 'Heart rate, beats/min', YA, columns BL, 30 min, 60 min

detail: Every value of a model marker (glucose, insulin, heart rate in Tables 2 and 3) is printed as mean ± a spread that no footnote, caption or methods sentence labels as SD or SEM (only Table 1 and the supplementary Table S1 are said to be mean ± SD); beyond that, the paper never states that subjects fasted before the morning meal, insulin is in pg/mL, and the middle-aged group (hypertension, dyslipidaemia, obesity, antihypertensive and statin use) cannot be represented.
